findings.evidence: Procedure step 1 requires testing to be reported as the subsection "of the pattern it tests", but the template places "### Testing Patterns" after "### Pattern 2" and "### Additional approaches" at the same heading level. With multiple approaches, the template does not establish which implementation the test belongs to.
findings.fix: Place a "#### Testing Patterns" subsection inside each applicable "### Pattern N" section, before the next pattern or Additional approaches, and update step 1 to use that heading level. Preserve the testing-only and missing-test branches.

findings.evidence: "Glob does not respect `.gitignore` by default ... (checked 2026-11-15)" states a vendor-tool default with a check date but no source URL or runtime-check instruction in the agent. The supporting URL exists in the audit fact ledger, which the agent does not reference. Facts were not verified online in this judgment.
findings.fix: Attach https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference to the tool-behavior claim alongside its existing checked date, retaining the Grep/Glob distinction and direct-path fallback.

findings.evidence: Quote code you did not read in this run, or invent a test when none exists: unverified quotes get copied into new code.
findings.fix: Keep the verbatim-quote rule; drop only the reason clause, which restates what the model already knows about copying unverified code, and record that removal in docs/audit/recovery/codebase-pattern-finder/record.md.

findings.evidence: When examples differ, describe the observed differences factually (for instance offset versus cursor pagination); do not say which is better.
findings.fix: The Never list already forbids ranking; delete this restatement, or move the offset-versus-cursor illustration into a bundled skill's references/ if callers ask for a pagination example, and record the removal.

findings.evidence: Cover the requested pattern types (feature, structural, integration, testing); if none is named, search one feature pattern plus Testing Patterns only.
findings.fix: The four types are named but never defined, so the search order is a checklist without a decision rule. Add one line that says how to tell them apart (feature = same behavior, structural = same file or type shape, integration = a call across a boundary, testing = the tests of that candidate) before the anchor search.

findings.evidence: Recommend, rank or call a pattern "preferred", "better" or "optimal": the caller decides, and an agent's guess would be mistaken for a repository convention.
findings.fix: The first Never bullet already gives the reason; the next three bullets (critique, unread quotes, reformatting) state the prohibition without a why. Add one clause each: a critique gets copied as a house rule, an unread quote becomes new code, a reformatted snippet is mistaken for the file's style.

findings.evidence: Show at most three approaches in file-path order (not by merit); list any further distinct approaches by `file:line` under "Additional approaches" without expanding or ranking them. Expand everything only if the caller asks for exhaustive coverage.
findings.fix: "Materially distinct" and the three-approach cap are two controls on the same choice. Keep the cap as the default and say a variant is distinct only when its control flow or data shape differs, not when only names differ.

findings.evidence: If still nothing, write one line per pattern type: "No match for <pattern type> in <scope searched>", placed under that pattern type's `## Pattern Examples` heading as its only content (omit the other sections for it).
findings.fix: That branch never says what to do with the other requested types that did match, and step 1's single-request testing case has no `## Pattern Examples` heading to put the line under. Say: emit the no-match line only for the types that failed, keep the matched types in the normal skeleton, and for a testing-only request put the line under `## Pattern Examples: Testing` with `### Testing Patterns` as its only subsection.
